name: Chuck Schumer

issue_poll.name: Marist Poll, New York registered voters, Oct 3–6, 2022; Pew Research national registered voters, Oct 10–16, 2022
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–6 from Marist's NY top-issue question, which offered six options. Ranks 7–10 are the next issues by share of voters calling them very important in Pew's national poll (https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2022/10/PP_2022.10.20_midterms-economy_REPORT.pdf), skipping items already listed; Pew's 'elections and voting' item merged into rank 2.

issues.position: Pointed to the Inflation Reduction Act; no new specific measure
Pass a comprehensive voting rights bill; oppose voter suppression
issues.note: The voting rights bill he backed got no floor vote; rated on the SAVE America Act.

issues.position: Pass Justice in Policing Act; schedule fentanyl without mandatory minimums

votes.bill_title: Disapproving D.C. Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Act
votes.question: On passage

issues.note: HALT Act adds mandatory minimums for fentanyl analogues; Yea inferred (84-16, all voted, not among named nays).

issues.position: Restore Roe protections in federal law; oppose a national ban

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: Procedural Nay so he could move to reconsider; he filed the cloture motion (Congressional Record).

issues.position: Make ACA coverage more affordable; expand Medicaid in all states

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: H.R.1 cut Medicaid and tightened ACA marketplace rules.

issues.position: Create a path to citizenship for millions of immigrants
issues.note: No floor vote on a path to citizenship this term.

issues.position: Cancel up to $50,000 in federal student debt

votes.bill_title: Disapproval of student loan debt relief
votes.question: On passage

issues.position: Cut carbon emissions at least 50%; 80% clean power grid
issues.note: H.R.1 phased out wind, solar and EV tax credits.

issues.position: Expand background checks; reinstate the assault weapons ban
issues.note: No recorded floor vote on background checks or an assault weapons ban this term.

issues.position: Said he was open to adding justices; no commitment

caveats: Abortion vote 211 is a leader's procedural Nay on a bill he backed; scored consistent, which senate.gov re-check will show as Nay.
Many positions come from an April 2022 LGBTQ Democratic club questionnaire (jimowles.org); his campaign site gave few specific forward commitments.
Ranks 7–10 use national Pew polling because the NY poll offered only six issues.
